data.title: Solutions Engineer
data.description:
Headquarters: United States
URL: https://www.backblaze.com

Solutions Engineer

Backblaze (Nasdaq: BLZE) | Remote, US | AI and application storage Solutions Engineering | Reports to the Solutions Engineering Manager (the VP of Solutions Engineering until the manager is hired) | Works with Account Executives, Product, Support, and the Solutions Engineering team

Salary range: $128,000-$144,000 plus variable pay and RSUs.

How We Got Here

We started by building storage servers from scratch in a Palo Alto apartment to save 90% on hardware. Turns out hard constraints make for pretty good engineering. That discipline forged a platform that performs as well or better than competitors, scales to multi-exabyte workloads, and costs a fraction of what AWS or Google charge. AI infrastructure runs on data. Storage gets hard at scale. We've been breaking, rebuilding, and improving that storage layer for 20 years.

Today, the world's leading AI infrastructure providers, neoclouds, and data-intensive businesses run on Backblaze. Our platform includes:

  • B2 Overdrive - high-throughput object storage engineered for AI infrastructure, GPU workloads, and massive-scale data pipelines
  • B2 Neo - white-label enterprise cloud storage powering neocloud platforms for AI, HPC, and media
  • B2 Cloud Storage - S3-compatible object storage with predictable pricing, free egress, and no lock-in
  • Computer Backup - automatic, continuous endpoint backup for Macs and PCs

500,000+ customers. 175 countries. Nasdaq: BLZE. backblaze.com

The Role

Backblaze sells a technical product, so Solutions Engineers join the deal at the first discovery conversation, before it is qualified. You will partner with Account Executives to learn what a customer needs, run the proof of concept that shows Backblaze fits, and stay close after the deal closes. This role focuses on AI and application storage customers.

Nearly every customer is replacing something they already run. Your job is to show where Backblaze slots into what they have already built, not to design their stack from scratch. You will earn trust by being curious, hands-on, and straight with customers about what the test shows.

This is not a demo-and-handoff role. If your instinct is to open a terminal, test a customer's real workload, and write down what you find, keep reading.

What You Will Do

  • Join discovery early. Work with the AE from the first conversation to learn the customer's workload, success criteria, and timeline.
  • Run proofs of concept. Define success with the customer, test Backblaze against what they run today, and report results plainly, including ones they didn't hope for.
  • Show where Backblaze fits. Explain how Backblaze slots into the customer's AI data pipeline alongside the compute, networking, and storage they already use.
  • Hand off cleanly. Take the lead through the technical win, then step back so the AE can carry the deal through negotiation.
  • Stay engaged after the sale. Answer questions in shared customer channels, help customers adopt the platform, and work with the AE on expansion.
  • Carry the field back to Product. Capture gaps and requests with evidence.
  • Share what you learn. Contribute benchmarks, technical content, and events.

What We Are Looking For

  • Curiosity. You dig into technical workflows and pick apart what customers tell you. This is the trait that matters most.
  • Programming fluency. You are comfortable in at least one language, any language, and use it to script tests and automate work.
  • Customer-facing experience. You have worked directly with customers in solutions engineering, support, technical account management, consulting, or a similar role. A sales background is not required.
  • Working knowledge of cloud infrastructure. You can explain how compute, storage, and networking fit into an AI data pipeline and where a storage layer sits. Experience on any cloud counts, whether AWS, Google, Azure, or CoreWeave. You don't need to have built these systems yourself.
  • Strong communication. You can explain a technical result clearly to an engineer or an executive, and you listen well.
  • Hands-on habits. You test things yourself and write down what you find.

Also True of the Right Person

  • Experience across a whole deal at a smaller company, from discovery through post-sale
  • Experience with object storage or the S3 API, or with AI and GPU workloads such as training, inference, and checkpointing
  • Familiarity with a sales qualification method such as MEDDPICC
  • Experience supporting customers after close, including expansions

This Is Not the Role for You If

  • You want to stay at the demo layer rather than test real workloads
  • You wait for an AE to ask before you engage
  • You see the job as finished at signature rather than after the customer is live

How We Will Interview

You will have four conversations: a recruiter screen, the hiring manager, our principal solutions architect, and a member of the Solutions Engineering team. We will ask you to walk us through a proof of concept you ran, including a result the customer did not hope for and how you reported it. We will ask about a technical problem you dug into yourself, and how you work with customers and Account Executives. 

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation and equity package
  • Full benefits including medical, dental, vision, and 401(k) with matching
  • RSU grants for full-time employees
  • ESPP program
  • Flexible vacation policy
  • Maternity & paternity leave

  • Childcare bonus (human children only)
  • Fertility treatment and support
  • Learning & development program
  • Commuter benefits
  • A collaborative and transparent culture that supports a healthy work-life balance

Pay Transparency and Equal Opportunity

To provide greater transparency to candidates, we share base pay ranges for all US-based job postings regardless of state. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials.

Salary range: $128,000-$144,000 plus variable pay and RSUs.

Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. 

About the OS Integration team:

The OS Integration team ensures Firefox works well with the host operating system and environment. We’re a distributed team with expertise in Windows, macOS, and Linux-based operating systems. Our responsibilities include developing fixes and improvements for Firefox related to Windows, macOS, and Linux environments. This might include integration with a new OS feature or fixing an OS-specific user interface bug. Other responsibilities include native crash reporting, OS abstraction layers, sandboxing, hardening, installer, updater, device APIs, and enterprise DLP support. 

About the role:

As a member of the OS Integration team, you’ll develop fixes, improvements, and new features for Firefox. The role will lean on your Windows expertise, but projects may have a cross-platform component. This role will include development of features for Firefox in enterprise environments especially implementation of Data Loss Prevention (DLP) features. As a Staff Software Engineer, you’re a clear communicator and expert in your domain, ready to work on multi-month projects. You’ll contribute to the team through code review, mentoring, and discussion.

  • Experience with desktop application development on Windows with C++.
  • Advanced knowledge of C and C++ and a solid understanding of assembly language such as x64, x86, or arm64.
  • Knowledge of web technologies such as Javascript, HTML, and CSS.
  • Knowledge of secure coding practices and memory safety concerns.
  • Strong problem-solving and debugging skills.
  • Written and verbal communication skills with a collaborative mindset.

data.title: Founding Product Engineer - Listen Labs
data.description:
Listen Labs

Everyone hates surveys. They’re tedious to fill out and give shallow data. That’s because they’re only a proxy for the real thing: conversations. Through a conversation, you can ask follow-up questions and get deep insights in a way that’s fun for the interviewee. Except you can’t have 1:1 conversations with everyone…

Listen Labs has built an AI interviewer that can ask follow-up questions, like a conversation, but at the scale and ease of use of a survey.

Technical Challenges

Turn qualitative data into quantitative insights

Listen Labs clusters free-form conversation into a structured format. This is not a trivial task. We use embeddings, fine-tuned large language models, and more to solve these problems.

Ask the right questions

Having a great conversation is not trivial. We’re fine-tuning and prompting in novel ways to get the right output from LLMs.

Multi-modality

We’ve built the fastest speech-to-speech pipeline but there’s a number of challenges we need to address to make it better. Our interviewer has audio input and output to the LLM and that’s tricky to get right.

Investors

There’s been $30B+ of market cap created from bringing surveys online. Our partner at Sequoia, [Bryan Schreier](https://www.sequoiacap.com/people/bryan-schreier/), was the first investor in Qualtrics – the $12B survey company.

About you

  • You love working on products end-to-end without detailed direction

  • You want to work in Next.js, TypeScript, and large language models

  • You are a collaborative builder and like to build systems with other engineers in mind.

  • You are an excellent written and verbal communicator.

  • You know when to seek assistance, and it's typically to discuss tradeoffs.

  • You don't scoff at unglamorous engineering tasks, yaks don't shave themselves.

  • Highly technical

  • Interested in building products end-to-end and owning the user experience

  • Excited about large language models

What we offer

  • $150,000 - $200,000 USD in cash.

  • High equity grant even for an early stage startup.

  • Work in person in our office @ 425 2nd St in San Francisco.

You will be the technical voice in the room from the first conversation. The team vets customization use cases on inbound leads before deals close, builds the agreed functionality after close, and turns the best of that work into capabilities every Luxury Presence customer can use.

This role pairs technical leadership with solution engineering. You will work directly with customers and sales to shape what we build, then lead the team that builds it.

Turn one-off builds into platform capabilities. Spot the solutions worth generalizing and graduate them into reusable capabilities for all customers, not only MMC.

Lead and grow the MMC team. Manage 2-4 direct reports. Own coaching, 1:1s, direct feedback, and career development. Treat management as a craft.

Who We Are

Our integrated solutions fit into existing workflows and give senior-living operators greater visibility into what is happening across their communities. Senior Software Engineer (Backend Applications)

We are a global digital innovation agency for the Intelligence Age, specializing in digital product development, brand transformation, media, and communications for major companies. Our Technology team is an integral part of our business; they are perpetual problem solvers, always seeking new and innovative ways to help our creatives bring their ideas to life. We work across a diverse range of projects, from major website builds and core tech platforms to bespoke experiences and strategic innovation with emerging technologies.

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer with a focus on backend applications to be part of our team servicing Google. This role will be responsible for building core services that power major global web experiences, with an emphasis on data ingestion, API design and implementation, and integrations. You’ll be comfortable with a variety of coding languages such as C++ and Python, and will design and scale low-latency RPC/REST microservices, architect globally distributed relational and vector database schemas, build resilient batch data-ingestion pipelines, and own automated CI/CD release workflows from prototype to production.

You will act as a core code contributor within a broader team, moving beyond simple feature implementation to architecting reusable systems, performing rigorous code reviews, and ensuring the seamless integration of diverse technologies. The ideal candidate is a specialist who understands the full software development lifecycle and is passionate about delivering high-quality, production-ready code in a collaborative environment.

Key Responsabilities

On any given day, you will:

  • Design & Evolve API Designs: Design, version, and maintain clean, backward-compatible gRPC and REST/HTTP APIs (supporting multi-version v1/v2 lifecycles), including request/response contracts, deadline budgets, stateless encrypted pagination, and data-governance annotations.
  • Build & Manage High-Performance Serving & Search Features: Build high-concurrency, low-latency backend handlers (using C++ primarily). Optimize hybrid retrieval pipelines that combine full-text search, real-time ML query embeddings, and vector search, with graceful degradation when upstream dependencies degrade.
  • Design Distributed Databases: Architect normalized and interleaved relational schemas, partitioned full-text search indexes, vector indexes, and incremental materialized views on a globally distributed SQL database. Design atomic snapshot/versioning patterns for zero-downtime data updates and instant rollbacks.
  • Manage Scalability & Batch Data Pipelines: Build and operate distributed ETL/batch ingestion pipelines that extract CMS content, perform HTML chunking and rate-limited ML embedding generation, validate data integrity, quarantine malformed records, and bulk-load snapshots at scale.
  • Handle CI/CD, Release Engineering & Observability: Maintain automated build, test, coverage, and progressive rollout pipelines (continuous presubmit, multi-day staging soak phases, and decoupled scheduled data syncs).
  • Collaborate with Frontend Dev & Product Teams: collaborate with other devs to assess product requirements, and translate those into technical specifications.
  • Work with a fullstack team: Collaborate with fullstack web engineers to deliver web experiences leveraging enterprise-grade CMS platforms with custom integrations.
  • Documentation & Technical Mapping: Create documentation to ensure technical clarity, supporting long-term maintenance and team scalability.

The Ideal Candidate

  • T-Shaped: You have deep expertise in system application development, but also possess a breadth of skills to collaborate and contribute effectively across web experiences, a variety of backend stacks, and infrastructure design.
  • Product Mindset: You don’t just build features; you build systems. You are passionate about understanding how the solutions you build serve broader product initiatives and outcomes and use product inputs to inform your architecture approach
  • Large-Scale Delivery: You understand the rigor that needs to go into delivering and maintaining scaled applications and core services for major brands, including release orchestration, working closely with QA to remediate issues, and working in an agile environment with a scaled team.
  • Detail-Oriented Craft: You possess a passion for product quality, ensuring that your code is not only functional but also clean, maintainable, and well-tested; and can work autonomously to hold yourself and your work to a high standard.
  • AI-Enabled: You’re comfortable leveraging AI code-assist tools to accelerate your workflow and are interested in integrating AI services where they add genuine value to work efficiency, productivity, and quality.
  • Always Learning: You proactively keep up with modern best practices and concepts, and constantly look for ways to incorporate new approaches into your daily work.

You Bring

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience building production backend services.
  • Systems Programming: Strong proficiency in modern C++ (C++17/20) and familiarity with Python and SQL.
  • API & Service Design: Proven experience designing versioned RPC (gRPC/Protobuf) and RESTful HTTP APIs, including pagination, input validation, error handling, and backward compatibility.
  • Database Design: Solid foundation in relational database modeling, indexing strategies, query optimization, and transaction/consistency models in distributed SQL systems.
  • CI/CD & Testing: Strong grasp of CI/CD concepts—hermetic unit/integration testing, code coverage, automated presubmits, canary deployments, staged rollouts, and rollback strategies.
  • High-Performance Concurrency: Experience with asynchronous/fiber-based concurrency models, parallel fan-out/fan-in execution, tail-latency optimization, and circuit-breaking/fallback patterns.
  • Search & ML Retrieval Systems: Hands-on experience with full-text search engines, dense vector embeddings, approximate/exact vector indexing, or hybrid ranking (e.g., Reciprocal Rank Fusion).
  • Data Pipelines & Streaming/Batch ETL: Experience building large-scale distributed batch pipelines (e.g., Flume, Beam, Spark) with rate-limited external RPC enrichment and dead-letter/quarantine handling.
  • Privacy & Security Engineering: Familiarity with cryptographic token handling (AEAD), strict PII/user-data access controls, automated TTL/wipeout policies, and auditable production data changes.

data.title: Storage Platform Engineer
data.description:
About the Role

Supabase runs millions of Postgres databases, and storage performance is now one of the biggest levers on how fast, reliable, and affordable they are. We're building a software-defined, NVMe-over-Fabrics storage platform underneath Supabase Postgres. Postgres stays unmodified, and the new layer delivers near-local-NVMe performance with the durability and flexibility of networked storage.

As the senior engineer driving storage, you'll own this effort end to end: the architecture and build-vs-buy decisions, integration into our compute platform, and operating the system in production.

Your first goal is raw Postgres I/O performance at scale. In the longer term, the layer you build will provide the block-level snapshots and copy-on-write clones behind database branching, fast restores, and instant resizes. Because it's software-defined, it will also travel with us as we expand beyond a single cloud provider into multi-cloud and colocated infrastructure.

This is a foundational, high-ownership role. You'll set the technical direction for storage at Supabase and help grow the team around it.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

  • Lead the architecture of Supabase's NVMe-oF storage platform, including evaluating and deciding between adopting existing software-defined storage and building on SPDK

  • Integrate networked block storage into our Kubernetes-based compute platform through CSI drivers and custom controllers, covering provisioning, attach/detach, resizing, and migration

  • Make Postgres fast on networked storage by profiling and tuning the full I/O path, from fsync, WAL, and checkpoints through the kernel block layer, NVMe/TCP, and the network

  • Design for durability and availability, including replication or erasure coding, failure domains, failover, and data-integrity verification

  • Build I/O isolation and QoS so that noisy neighbors can't degrade other tenants

  • Set performance and reliability SLOs, and build the benchmarking and observability to hold the system to them

  • Design the layer for block-level snapshots and copy-on-write clones, laying the groundwork for database branching

  • Keep the platform portable across AWS, other clouds, and bare-metal/colo

  • Write design docs, mentor engineers, and work closely with the Compute, Branching, Postgres, and Multicloud teams

  • Participate in on-call rotations, incident response, and post-incident reviews

  • Resolve escalated support issues, while also identifying and resolving systemic issues across the platform

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

Must have:

  • Have 7+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time building and operating storage systems in production

  • Have built or operated distributed or software-defined block storage (for example Ceph RBD, Lightbits, Simplyblock, Portworx, LINSTOR/DRBD, or an in-house system)

  • Have hands-on experience with NVMe/TCP or NVMe-oF, including targets, initiators, multipath, and failover behavior

  • Have a deep understanding of Linux storage internals: the block layer, io_uring, page cache, O_DIRECT and fsync semantics, filesystems, and device-mapper

  • Write strong systems code in Go, plus C, C++, or Rust

  • Measure performance rigorously with fio, pgbench, eBPF, and perf, and can explain latency down to its individual components

  • Understand durability tradeoffs between replication, erasure coding, and consistency under failure

  • Have led technical direction on a complex system: design docs, tradeoffs, and bringing others along

  • Have experience with Kubernetes controllers and/or CSI drivers

  • Have been on call for large production systems

  • Communicate clearly in writing and thrive in async, globally distributed teams

Nice to have:

  • SPDK development experience

  • RDMA/RoCE experience

  • Experience implementing block-level snapshots, thin provisioning, or copy-on-write cloning

  • Postgres internals knowledge (WAL, buffer manager, checkpointer), or familiarity with OrioleDB

  • Experience with AWS networking and instance storage at scale (ENA, placement, bandwidth limits)

  • Experience running storage on bare metal or in colo

  • Contributions to open source storage projects or the Linux kernel storage stack

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

data.title: Staff Software Engineer (Interfaces)
data.description:
Headquarters: Remote

About the Team

As a Staff Software Engineer at Netlify, you'll join a collaborative team that values continuous learning, mutual support, and shared growth. Together, we create tools that help developers build faster, more intuitively, and with greater impact. Our Experience team owns the core product experience at Netlify, which is every way a human or an agent interacts with the platform, from our React-based web application to CLI, MCP, SDK, and API. If users interact with it directly, it's likely ours. We're reimagining how developers experience web development by thoughtfully integrating AI into our workflows - not as a novelty, but as a practical tool that enhances how we build the web.

With our team, you'll help set technical direction for our product area, mentor a highly senior team of engineers, and shape user experiences that serve millions of developers. You'll work closely with Product, Design, and engineering leadership, and partner with teams across the organization to build, iterate, and scale meaningful solutions. You'll have the autonomy to guide what we build and how, and the influence to bring others along with you, all while staying hands-on in the codebase.

We're looking for thoughtful engineers who enjoy owning problems end to end, collaborating across disciplines, and solving complex technical challenges for products that millions of developers rely on every day. AI is a foundational part of how we build, so we value engineers who are excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI-assisted workflows while continuing to apply strong engineering fundamentals. We believe the best engineering happens when talented people are trusted to solve difficult problems together, share what they're learning, and create space for different perspectives to shape better solutions.  With our team, you'll have real ownership from day one - not a tiny slice of a massive codebase. Engineers here are trusted to make decisions, shape technical direction, and move quickly while collaborating closely with Product and Design.

What You'll Do

  • Use your deep expertise in full-stack development (TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, and React) to ship reliable, scalable, performant code across our product suite, and set the patterns that others on the team and across the org follow. 
  • Own the technical direction for our product area, including the web app, CLI, MCP, SDK, API, and docs, by defining architecture and roadmap alongside your manager, Product, and Design, and make tradeoffs explicit so decisions are easy to understand and revisit
  • Lead large, ambiguous projects that span multiple teams from conception to delivery, such as our application rewrite and upcoming CLI rework, writing RFCs, driving alignment, and managing risk and timelines
  • Design and evolve user-facing features and product APIs for both humans and agents, recognizing that the best interface isn’t always a React application. Build them to scale to millions of developers worldwide, with a clear view of reliability, performance, and long-term maintainability.
  • Make thoughtful product and interface decisions on your own with the overall customer experience top of mind
  • Set the bar for engineering practices - testing, documentation, observability, and performance optimization - and lead how the team pragmatically uses AI tools, sharing what works and what doesn't
  • Turn ambiguity into clear plans, guiding both early-stage prototypes and production-ready applications that directly impact user experience and business metrics
  • Mentor and grow engineers through code reviews, design reviews, pairing, and sponsorship, raising the technical level of the whole team
  • Practice proactive async communication and create visibility across projects by documenting your workflows and decision-making clearly
  • Participate in on-call rotations, lead incident follow-up, and drive continuous improvement efforts that reduce technical debt and prevent recurring problems
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and engineering leadership to shape user flows that enhance the developer experience across our platform, and contribute to hiring and team growth

What You'll Bring

  • Deep expertise in TypeScript and JavaScript, with a long track record of designing, shipping, and maintaining production-quality software in modern full-stack environments
  • A history of building interfaces developers use directly, such as web apps, CLIs, APIs, SDKs, or other dev tools, and a strong sense of what works well for developers (and, by extension, agents)
  • Passion for building strong user-facing experiences, including working with React and modern frontend architecture and making architectural decisions that hold up as products and teams grow, paired with the backend knowledge to design software well beyond the UI
  • Strong product and design instincts. This isn’t about visual polish - it’s about making thoughtful decisions about how users interact with a product.
  • Strong proficiency with Go and/or Ruby for backend services and API development, with a thoughtful approach to reliability and performance
  • Hands-on experience with React and modern frontend architecture, including making architectural decisions that hold up as products and teams grow
  • Demonstrated ability to raise the technical bar: providing direction to senior and staff-level engineers, distributing ownership, mentoring, shaping standards, and influencing decisions beyond your own team
  • Extensive experience delivering features and services that serve large user bases, including designing for scale and operating systems in production
  • A track record of leading technically complex, cross-team projects from ambiguous problem to shipped outcome, including writing RFCs and building consensus
  • Demonstrated ability to raise the technical bar: mentoring senior and mid-level engineers, shaping standards, and influencing decisions beyond your own team
  • Experience writing high-quality, testable code that's reliable and maintainable over time, and setting that expectation for others
  • Proficiency using and experimenting with AI-assisted development tools, with sound judgment about when and how to apply them and the ability to help others do the same
  • Experience contributing to open-source projects or working in public codebases is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially in asynchronous, remote-first environments, with the ability to explain tradeoffs to engineers, leadership, and non-technical partners
  • Critical thinking abilities and a solution-oriented approach to complex technical challenges, with the judgment to prioritize and say no when needed
  • A collaborative approach to problem-solving with curiosity about how your work supports teammates, users, and broader goals
  • Growth mindset and openness to learning new tools, technologies, and best practices
  • Passion for working in a collaborative environment with diverse teams across distributed locations

This Role is a Great Fit If

  • You're energized by building user-facing products and features that directly impact millions of developers' daily workflows
  • You thrive in collaborative environments, working closely with your team and cross-functionally to turn ideas into reality
  • You enjoy the autonomy and influence of staff-level work - setting technical direction, writing RFCs, and driving decisions across teams while staying connected to the people doing the work
  • You find satisfaction in making other engineers better, whether through mentoring, design reviews, or setting a clear example
  • You see ambiguity as a creative opportunity and can navigate uncertainty to build practical solutions and bring clarity to others
  • You see AI as a multiplier for your skills, not a shortcut, and can articulate where it helps, where it doesn't, and how you use it
  • You're excited by new tools, challenges, and opportunities to grow, even when they feel a little uncomfortable at first
  • You want to work on a fully remote team that believes in autonomy, transparency, and building a better web, together

Applying

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Please apply anyway!

When applying please include: 

A resume or short listing of your job history & skills (link to a LinkedIn profile would be fine). We appreciate a cover letter explaining why you would enjoy working in this role at Netlify to get to know you a bit better, though this is not required and will not impact your application. Our mission is to “build a better web” and that cannot be done without a diversity of skill sets, backgrounds and thoughts. 

Of everything we've ever built at Netlify, we are most proud of our team. Netlify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are devoted to building a team of people with diverse backgrounds and lifestyles. Driving equality empowers our team, enables us to innovate, and helps us maintain a more inclusive environment. We don’t discriminate against employees or applicants based on gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, race, military/veteran status, citizenship, pregnancy status, or any other differences. If we can do anything to provide a better interview, i.e. accommodate a disability, then please let us know by emailing accommodations@netlify.com. 

About Netlify

Netlify is a platform that lets you create, share, and run anything on the web: a website, an app, an agent experience, whatever you can dream up. Use your own tools or ours to build it, collaborate with your team, get it live, and keep it running. Anyone, from people just starting out to seasoned developers, can create pro-level web experiences that really work, really well.

We are a Series D company that has raised over $200M from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, EQT, Bessemer, BOND, and Menlo Ventures. As a fully distributed company, we aim to create a company culture where the best idea can come from anywhere and strive to be thoughtful, compassionate, and collaborative in our work. If this sounds like something you’d like to be part of, we’re excited to connect with you!

At Netlify, we are committed to a compensation philosophy that prioritizes fairness and equity, positions our employee compensation competitively in the market, recognizes and rewards performance, and takes a comprehensive approach to our rewards package. We anchor our compensation philosophy on a market-based approach, therefore salary ranges may differ depending on the labor cost in a particular location. The salary provided is in addition to robust benefits and participation in Netlify’s equity plan. Our hiring range for this role is targeted at $182,000 - $248,000 for most US-based locations, $175,000 - $235,000 CAD in most Canada-based locations, and £105,000 – £144,000 GBP for most UK-based locations.  Candidates outside the US, Canada, UK, or in premium markets should consult with their Talent Acquisition partner regarding location-based ranges, as they may be higher or lower than the average US range listed. The starting pay will be determined based on multiple factors, including expertise and skills, market demands, experience, internal equity, and applicable geographic location. These compensation packages and ranges are subject to change and may be modified in the future.

data.title: Designer - AI Organisations
data.description:
About the Company

The OpenAI Deployment Company ("DeployCo") is the deployment arm of OpenAI, purpose-built to deliver enterprise AI transformation at scale. As model capabilities accelerate, deployment has become the primary constraint to realizing AI value creation within large enterprises. DeployCo bridges that gap.

Our ambition is to build the company that defines AI deployment. We operate at the intersection of cutting-edge AI, enterprise transformation, and scaled services delivery. We partner with enterprise customers to identify where AI can transform their businesses and build solutions leveraging OpenAI's models and products. We work with many of the world's largest and most influential companies to solve their most complex business challenges using the latest advances in AI.

People who thrive at DeployCo get excited about ambitious and complex work. We are deep believers in the future with AI. We execute quickly, value intellectual honesty and empathy, and obsess over the solutions we build for our customers.

DeployCo is being built from the ground up as a subsidiary of OpenAI and funded with a partnership of outside investors.

About the Role

We are seeking a designer who combines human-centred design with technical AI expertise to help people discover what AI makes possible, build useful AI-enabled workflows, and help leaders reshape how their organisations work around this technology.

Our design capability shapes AI products and experiences for customers and employees, and helps organisations rethink how people, teams and AI work together. Our ‘AI Organisations’ work focuses on closing the gap between what AI can do and the value businesses get from it, addressing the human and organisational changes needed alongside engineering and AI product delivery.

We help people explore what’s possible through experimentation on work they understand, building curiosity, confidence and judgement. Alongside this, we work with leaders and teams to test how roles, structures and working practices could change, creating the conditions for AI-empowered teams to thrive.

You might come from service design, organisation design, human-centred design or a technology innovation background. You’ll have hands-on experience using AI to prototype and improve workflows, and be interested in building human-AI organisations: shaping how people and AI work together.

Your day-to-day will include helping teams identify where AI can make a difference, co-designing and building working AI-enabled workflows and product prototypes, and refining them through use and feedback. You’ll facilitate hands-on learning and work alongside leaders and colleagues to embed these solutions into everyday work and design and test new ways of organising work, using AI. You’ll combine design craft, technical judgement and an understanding of human behaviour to turn new capabilities into practical, lasting changes.

This role is based in Singapore, with hybrid work and customer travel shaped by deployment needs.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and facilitate AI experiences that expand what people believe is possible. Use play, guided experimentation and reflection on familiar work to help people try unfamiliar approaches, challenge results and discuss uncertainty.

  • Help participants turn their discoveries into practical ideas for their own work. Design activities and learning materials that support different levels of technical confidence and help people move from exploration to action.

  • Work alongside teams to make ChatGPT and Codex useful in everyday work. Understand their tasks, identify promising workflows and help them build confidence through hands-on use.

  • Configure tools, prototype AI-enabled workflows and products, and build useful connections to existing systems. Work with engineers where deeper integration is needed, using observation and feedback from teams to refine the solutions and how work gets done.

  • Contribute to AI transformation by helping leaders and teams examine job roles, routines, decision rights, structures, incentives and physical spaces as AI takes a more active role.

  • Design new ways of working with the people whose work will change. Make the implications tangible through prototypes and experiments, helping leaders decide what to adopt, adapt or investigate further.

You may thrive in this role if you:

Bring technical expertise

  • Understand how AI tools work, their capabilities and limitations, and their implications in real working environments.

  • Configure AI tools for specific tasks and prototype connections to external systems using APIs and integrations.

  • Exercise judgement on feasibility, reliability and data permissions, recognising when specialist engineering support is needed.

Understand human & organisational behaviour

  • Use research to understand people’s motivations, habits and concerns, including what builds confidence and trust in AI.

  • Connect technical possibilities with organisational culture, structures, incentives and working relationships.

  • Help people try new practices through practical guidance, hands-on support and feedback, so they build confidence and retain judgement as their work changes.

Are skilled in facilitation and learning enablement

  • Design and facilitate workshops and experiences grounded in participants’ own work.

  • Make technical ideas accessible, creating space for curiosity and constructive challenge across different skill levels.

  • Help people reflect on discoveries, identify useful applications and move from exploration to action.

Have AI product fluency

  • Know ChatGPT and Codex thoroughly and help people discover relevant applications for their work.

  • Help people use instructions, context and iteration effectively, and assess the quality of their AI outputs.

  • Keep pace with product developments and translate useful capabilities into practical demonstrations and experiments.

Apply workflow and human systems design

  • Map workflows and services, connecting customer and colleague experiences with the tasks, decisions, systems and structures behind them.

  • Redesign processes, roles, team structures and incentives around AI, making responsibilities, coordination and human judgement clear.

  • Prototype and test changes with the people affected, evaluating their impact and connecting team-level experiments to wider organisational change.

data.title: Staff Software Engineer, Search Core
data.description:
Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next.

We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.

Why You'll Love This Role

Cribl Search powers high-speed investigations for security and IT teams at some of the world's largest enterprises. Whether data lives in Lakehouse Engines or is spread across Federated sources, Search unifies ingest, storage, and analysis into a single experience — no tool-hopping, no complex orchestration. Teams collect once, search anywhere, and investigate with no blind spots.

Now add agentic AI to the picture. AI-driven workloads are exploding, autonomous agents are firing queries alongside human analysts, and the volume and complexity of concurrent searches is growing fast. The query engine at the heart of Cribl Search needs to be faster, more concurrent, and more resilient than ever — and that's where you come in.

Cribl is looking for a backend-focused Staff Software Engineer to join a remote-first, diverse, inclusive, cross-functional team of software developers focused on making search stupid fast. You will play a central role in evolving the query engine at the heart of Cribl Search – breaking through concurrency ceilings, optimizing query dispatching and execution, and tuning performance for workloads ranging from interactive analyst investigations to AI agents firing thousands of concurrent queries. This is an ideal role for anyone who is passionate about making Search blazing fast at a massive scale.

On top of it all, you will have fun! Cribl strives to be a great place to work for everyone.


As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will …

  • Contribute to technical direction, bringing strong, loosely held, opinions to shape how Cribl Search evolves as a platform for multiple products
  • Own high-impact changes to large-scale systems, increasing performance and concurrency for both human and AI-driven agentic workloads
  • ​​Build and support a strong foundation for Cribl Search as a whole, collaborating across various teams and divisions
  • Champion improvements to performance, reliability, and operability
  • Drive clarity across multiple stakeholders and ambiguous requirements, communicating tradeoffs and risks of competing priorities
  • Partner with leadership to translate organizational needs from across the business into actionable plans on our roadmap
  • Lead projects end-to-end – from ideation, scoping and design through implementation, testing, deployment, and production support
  • Mentor and coach engineers through design reviews, code reviews, and pairing
  • Write clean, maintainable, and testable code with an eye toward observability and resilience
  • Share on-call responsibilities as part of a team that embraces service ownership
  • Help define and refine the software development practices that make our team effective – everybody’s feedback helps shape our process 
  • We are a remote-first company and work happens across many time-zones – this position will require stand-by, on-call, or off-hours duties 


If You've Got - We Want It

  • Strong experience designing and operating multiple-petabyte-scale data systems, including object and distributed storage
  • Experience building search, query, and/or analytic systems working with structured and unstructured data
  • Deep understanding of how search tools work – indexing, inverted indices, query parsing, and execution (think Lucene/Solr, Elasticsearch)
  • Experience working on high-performance, data-intensive applications where concurrency, throughput, and latency matter
  • Familiarity with compilers, ASTs, and query language internals
  • Polyglot engineer – C++ experience is highly desirable
  • Ability to problem-solve from first principles and maintain focus on overarching objectives
  • Demonstrated ability to lead projects through ambiguity, driving technical decisions across team boundaries
  • Experience working in a fast paced, dynamic environment where priorities shift quickly
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written – able to explain complex technical topics to stakeholders in remote, distributed environments
  • Experience mentoring engineers and raising the technical bar on a team
  • Experience with C++, Typescript/JavaScript, NodeJS, and SQL

data.description:

Why You’ll Love This Role

Cribl is looking for a Principal Product Security Engineer to serve as a hands-on technical authority at the intersection of application, cloud, and FedRAMP environment security. You will help secure Cribl’s cloud-native, customer-managed, and hybrid products as they process high-volume data for some of the world’s largest organizations.

As a Principal engineer, impact is defined by reach. You will set long-term direction across teams, resolve critical and ambiguous security problems, advise Engineering and Product leaders, and turn security requirements into secure designs, production-ready patterns, automation, and verified outcomes. This is not a documentation-only compliance role: you will work with Engineering, SRE, Cloud Operations, Compliance, and Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) partners to make regulatory commitments real in product architecture and day-to-day operations.

This is a remote, hands-on individual-contributor role within Engineering. You will lead through expertise and influence, mentor engineers and security partners, and create durable systems that reduce risk while making the secure path easier.


As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will…

  • Set long-term product and cloud security direction across multiple teams, shaping roadmaps, standards, secure-by-default patterns, and risk-informed design and release decisions.
  • Lead Product Security Reviews for distributed, multi-tenant SaaS and customer-managed products, including architecture and design review, threat modeling, abuse-case analysis, targeted secure code review, and security test planning.
  • Translate risk into concrete engineering requirements, mitigations, tests, and secure defaults; stay engaged through implementation and independently verify that the intended risk reduction was achieved.
  • Serve as a principal cloud security authority across IAM and workload identity, organization and account boundaries, network exposure, KMS and encryption, secrets, logging and detection, containers and Kubernetes, serverless services, infrastructure as code, hardening, and data isolation.
  • Lead the Product Security component of FedRAMP engineering. Translate FedRAMP Moderate and NIST SP 800-53 control intent into sustainable technical controls and defensible evidence, and partner on authorization-boundary and significant-change decisions, continuous monitoring, vulnerability and change management, POA&M and deviation remediation, incident response, vendor assessments, and 3PAO or assessor interactions.
  • Investigate ambiguous signals and vulnerabilities from bug bounty, application and supply-chain scanners, penetration tests, cloud detections, and internal reports; determine exploitability, exposure, and impact; coordinate remediation; validate fixes and bypasses; and hunt for variants and root causes.
  • Evolve scalable, risk-adaptive vulnerability management using exposure, exploitability, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities signals, asset criticality, customer impact, and regulatory timelines,not CVSS alone.
  • Build and operate durable security capabilities and developer paved roads across CI/CD, SAST, SCA, secrets, infrastructure as code, containers, cloud posture, and testing. Automate repeatable work while preserving explicit human judgment for consequential security decisions.
  • Scope and oversee external penetration tests, purple-team exercises, and relevant security vendors; ensure findings become owned, verified engineering outcomes; and provide evidence-based input to build, retain, replace, or retire decisions.
  • Lead multi-team work through uncertainty and high-stakes situations, making clear tradeoffs among security, reliability, delivery, customer impact, and compliance while acting with appropriate urgency.
  • Communicate complex risks, options, uncertainty, and recommendations in direct, audience-appropriate terms for engineers, senior leaders, customers, assessors, and external partners; represent Cribl credibly when needed.
  • Multiply the team by mentoring Product Security engineers, security champions, and engineering partners; create standards, runbooks, automation, and continuity plans that prevent critical capabilities from depending on one person.
  • Evaluate and responsibly apply emerging technologies, including AI-assisted security engineering, with measurable outcomes, rigorous verification, secure operating boundaries, and clear human accountability.
  • This position will require stand-by, on-call, or off-hours duties.


If You’ve Got It - We Want It

  • Typically 10+ years of relevant software security, security engineering, or software engineering experience,or equivalent demonstrated scope and impact,including substantial hands-on Application Security or Product Security and cloud security work.
  • Experience securing AI or agentic systems and applying AI responsibly to security engineering workflows.
  • A Principal-level track record of setting technical direction across teams, leading multi-quarter initiatives, resolving ambiguous critical problems, and influencing senior Engineering and Product leaders without direct authority.
  • Deep, hands-on AWS and Azure security experience in production SaaS or cloud-native systems, including identity and authorization, network controls, encryption and key management, secrets, logging and detection, containers or Kubernetes, serverless services, infrastructure as code, and multi-tenant data isolation.
  • Direct experience implementing or operating product and cloud security controls in a FedRAMP-authorized or FedRAMP-bound environment. You understand NIST SP 800-53 control intent and have supported technical control implementation and evidence, continuous monitoring, vulnerability and change management, POA&M or deviation remediation, and assessor interactions.
  • Expertise leading security design reviews and threat models for complex applications, APIs, distributed systems, and cloud architectures, with the judgment to turn findings into practical countermeasures and risk-informed release recommendations.
  • Strong knowledge of web and application vulnerabilities, exploit techniques, OWASP guidance, authentication and authorization protocols, cryptography, common network protocols, and secure cloud operating models.
  • Ability to read production code and build maintainable automation in JavaScript or TypeScript, Python, Go, or a comparable language; willingness to work directly with Engineering to implement and verify security improvements.
  • Hands-on vulnerability-response experience, including exploitability analysis, root-cause and variant analysis, remediation design, fix and bypass validation, stakeholder coordination, and incident support.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the ability to make complex risk and tradeoffs clear to engineers, executives, customers, assessors, and external partners.
  • A bachelor’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience.
  • Preferred qualifications
    • Experience securing enterprise data platforms, observability systems, high-volume data pipelines, agents, or customer-managed and hybrid software.
    • Experience with AWS GovCloud, FedRAMP Moderate/High, NIST 800-53.
    • Experience building developer security platforms, secure-by-default libraries, policy-as-code, or automated guardrails across SAST, SCA, DAST, software supply chain, containers, and cloud posture.
    • Public security contributions such as open-source work, published research, CVE credits, standards participation, conference talks, or other demonstrated thought leadership.
    • Relevant credentials such as AWS Certified Security – Specialty, CISSP, CCSP, CSSLP, GIAC, or OSCP; demonstrated practical impact matters more than certifications.

data.title: Senior Customer Engineer, AI-Factory
data.description:
About the Company

Armada is the hyperscaler for the edge, delivering modular AI infrastructure from first deployment to AI factory with speed, scale and sovereignty. Named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and to the CNBC Disruptor 50, Armada’s solutions are deployed in over 60 countries globally for organizations ranging from energy to defense.

With nearly $500 million in funding to date, Armada is backed by leading investors including Founders Fund, Lux, BlackRock and Microsoft (M12), alongside strategic partnerships with Microsoft, Dell, Palantir, NVIDIA, SpaceX, and Skydio. We are building the infrastructure layer for sovereign and edge AI - rugged, deployable compute for customers that cannot rely on centralized cloud.

Working at Armada means taking ownership, driving autonomy, and delivering impact. You’ll tackle challenges that haven’t been solved before and help build something transformative from the ground up. What you do here will not only define your career but help further Armada’s mission to bridge the digital divide for customers around the world.

About the Role

The AI Factory Customer Engineer plays a pivotal role in bridging the gap between customer modular AI-ready data center requirements and Armada's Product and Engineering teams. This role requires deep technical credibility, hands-on infrastructure experience, and strong interpersonal skills to translate complex AI infrastructure and data center architectures into clear, practical solutions for customers looking to deploy sovereign AI infrastructure at speed.

This role goes beyond traditional pre-sales. The Customer Engineer acts as the technical interface between high-profile customers and Armada Engineering, ensuring customer requirements, constraints, and feedback are accurately represented and incorporated into solution design and future platform evolution.

Armada's AI Factory serves a broad and growing set of customers across enterprise, industrial, and infrastructure-heavy verticals. A meaningful and growing subset of strategic targets includes AI-focused datacenter co-location providers and Neocloud operators which represent a primary segment where Armada's high-density, liquid-cooled modular solutions are a compelling fit for capacity expansion and rapid deployment. Additionally, renewable energy operators who own or control significant land, power, and stranded energy assets are increasingly positioned to host or operate AI compute infrastructure at scale.

The ideal candidate brings an engineering and customer-first mindset, strong data center and AI-ready infrastructure expertise, particularly around AI, HPC, liquid-cooling, modular data center solutions, Nvidia reference architectures, along with the energy, curiosity, and positivity required to operate in a fast-moving, hyper-growth environment. This role is instrumental in driving adoption, trust, and long-term success for Armada's AI Factory modular solutions.

Location

Australia (Remote)

What You'll Do — Key Responsibilities

Core Technical Customer Engagement

  • Act as the primary technical interface between customers and Armada's Product and Engineering teams, translating real-world requirements into actionable technical inputs.
  • Provide expert technical guidance to Armada's AI Factory customers, including Modular Data Center (MDC)solutions, high-density and liquid-cooled designs, and GPU-based reference architectures created with partners such as NVIDIA.
  • Understand customer workloads and objectives deeply and advise on solution details including rack-level design, systems architectures, cooling and power draw advisory, and deployment strategy tradeoffs.
  • Lead technical demonstrations and workshops, tailoring content to customer constraints and operational realities.
  • Cultivate trusted-advisor relationships with customer engineering, infrastructure, IT, OT, and security stakeholders and teams
  • Engage with solution partners and supply chain, including MEP, OEM, xPU vendors, in service to end-to-end customer solutions
  • Enable field and sales teams by simplifying complex technical concepts into clear, customer-relevant narratives
  • Support RFI/P and ongoing customer-facing technical documentation required to support lighthouse customer requirements
  • Bring a high-ownership, self-starting mindset with the energy and curiosity to fill gaps, solve problems, and drive outcomes end-to-end.

AI Datacenter Co-Lo & Neocloud Engagement

  • Engage AI-focused datacenter co-location operators and Neocloud providers as a critical customer segment, positioning Armada's AI Factory as a solution for rapid capacity expansion, modular overflow deployments, and high-density liquid-cooled compute environments.
  • Develop sufficient familiarity with co-lo and Neocloud operational models — GPU cluster economics, high-density power and cooling requirements, multi-tenant compute, and deployment velocity expectations — to hold credible technical conversations and scope solutions appropriately.
  • Collaborate with Sales to identify where AI Factory's modular, rapidly deployable infrastructure is most differentiated against co-lo and Neocloud alternatives, and tailor technical positioning accordingly.

Renewable Energy & Land-and-Power Operator Engagement

  • Engage renewable energy operators, independent power producers, and upstream oil and gas companies (e.g., Chord Energy, Devon Energy, and similar) as a strategic and growing customer segment for Armada's AI Factory — helping them understand how their existing power generation capacity, land assets, and fiber infrastructure make them natural hosts for modular AI compute deployments.
  • Articulate the value proposition of Armada's MDC platform to energy sector operators: rapid deployment timelines, self-contained power and cooling architecture, scalable capacity, and the ability to monetize stranded or excess power assets through AI compute hosting.
  • Develop familiarity with the operational model of energy companies: power generation economics, land and lease structures, regulatory constraints, and the OT/IT boundary — and translate these into informed AI Factory deployment conversations.
  • Navigate both the OT and IT stakeholder landscape within energy companies, building credibility with infrastructure, operations, and executive teams alike.
  • Identify and communicate the specific deployment considerations relevant to energy sector environments: remote or off-grid locations, variable power availability, environmental and permitting requirements, and physical security constraints.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Field Strategy

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Product, and Engineering to support customer engagements, technical scoping, and solution design across all target verticals.
  • Stay current on industry trends related to AI infrastructure, energy sector AI adoption, data center design, liquid cooling, and modular systems — and share insights internally to shape future product strategy.
  • Attend industry events and conferences, representing Armada with customers, partners, and industry insiders
  • Bring positive energy, curiosity, and a collaborative mindset to every engagement — this role values technical excellence and having fun while building something meaningful.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent hands-on engineering experience). Advanced engineering degrees are a plus.
  • 10-15+ years of relevant experience in data center engineering, infrastructure engineering, pre-sales, sales engineering, or solution architecture roles.
  • Strong understanding of compute, networking, and storage fundamentals, including AI and GPU-based systems
  • Hands-on experience with mechanical, electrical, thermal, advanced cooling and networking components of data center solutionsFamiliarity with modular data centers (MDCs) landscape
  • Engineering mindset with curiosity about what lives inside the rack, including openness to evolving beyond current AI and HPE reference designs (e.g., B300 / GB300) as architectures evolve.
  • Familiarity with foundational cloud platforms, containerization, virtualization, and modern enterprise infrastructure.
  • Ability to navigate and build credibility with technical infrastructure buying personas at all levels
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and comfort operating in complex, live customer environments.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage both highly technical engineers and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Willingness to travel as required.

About Osano:

Osano is an innovative B-Corporation built around a simple belief: privacy is a fundamental right. Since day one, we’ve been focused on giving modern enterprises the ability to innovate quickly, stay competitive, and earn customer trust by respecting data privacy and complying with consent guidelines. Our products help organizations operate confidently in a rapidly evolving regulatory and technological landscape.

About the Role:

Reporting to Executive leadership, the Sr. Manager of IT & Operations owns Osano's internal technology environment day to day. This role runs IT operations, manages the corporate technology stack, and improves systems, security, and employee experience over time. The ideal candidate is hands-on, operationally excellent, and ready to take on more strategic ownership as the company grows.

Core Responsibilities

Operations and Systems Ownership:

  • Own and continuously improve Osano's internal IT operations, including endpoint management, identity and access, SaaS administration, and corporate infrastructure.
  • Keep systems reliable and employees productive.

IT Roadmap Execution:

  • Maintain and deliver a near-term IT roadmap aligned with company growth. Identify gaps, prioritize improvements, and ship them consistently.

Budget and Vendor Management:

  • Manage the IT and corporate technology budget.
  • Own vendor relationships, renewals, and contract negotiations to control cost and remove redundant tools.

Security and Compliance:

  • Serve as the internal technical lead for SOC 2 IT audit evidence and controls.

Stakeholder Support:

  • Partner with department leads and the executive team to resolve operational bottlenecks and support the needs of a growing, distributed team.

Technical Scope

Identity and Access Management:

  • Administer and secure Google Workspace and corporate identity infrastructure.
  • Manage SSO, SAML configurations, conditional access policies, and endpoint security across Mac, Windows, and mobile devices, using EDR tooling including Microsoft Defender and Iru Avert.

Automation and Lifecycle Management:

  • Build and maintain automation for onboarding, offboarding, and hardware provisioning using low-code tools, Google Apps Script, Bash, or PowerShell.

AI Tool Governance:

  • Establish and enforce policies for safe, compliant adoption of AI tools across the organization.

Documentation and Training:

In this role, you’ll leverage AI to create and maintain documentation, resolve routine support requests more efficiently, build automations, and identify recurring ticket trends and opportunities for improvement.

data.description:
Headquarters: Remote, Massachusetts, United States, AMER

From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us


Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data. Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on. Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions. As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact. During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

Fivetran + dbt  is seeking a Manager of Security Operations, Incident Detection and Response, to bolster and improve the robustness and security of the platform and the entire enterprise. This people-leadership role is hands-on and execution-focused, requiring deep expertise in security operations, incident detection and response, AI-driven security automation, and securing multi-tenant SaaS environments. You'll build and lead a high-performing team, own the detection and response technology stack, and serve as the accountable leader for incident response across the entire enterprise, ensuring threats are detected, contained, and remediated quickly from endpoint to cloud to production.

This is a full-time remote position based out of the US (EST Time Zone).

Technologies You’ll Use

Crowdstrike, Okta, Google Workspace, Wiz, Open Source, Notion, JIRA

What You’ll Do

  • People Leadership: Lead, mentor, and develop a team of detection and response engineers and analysts. Set clear goals, manage performance, and grow careers while fostering a culture of ownership, curiosity, and urgency.
  • Hiring & Team Building: Recruit, hire, and onboard top security talent. Define team structure, roles, on-call rotations, and hiring plans to scale the team alongside the business.
  • Enterprise Incident Response: Own the incident response program for the entire enterprise, including investigation, containment, eradication, remediation, and post-incident review. Act as incident commander for major security events and coordinate with Legal, Privacy, Communications, and executive leadership.
  • Detection Engineering: Build, optimize, and maintain high-fidelity detections across cloud, identity, endpoint, SaaS, and application layers, using threat-informed approaches such as MITRE ATT&CK to close coverage gaps.
  • AI-Driven Security Operations: Drive the adoption of AI, including LLMs and AI agents, to automate alert triage, enrichment, investigation, and response. Evaluate and integrate AI capabilities to scale the team, and build detections for threats targeting AI systems and AI usage across the enterprise.
  • Multi-Tenant SaaS Security: Design detection and response strategies tailored to a multi-tenant SaaS platform, including tenant isolation, cross-tenant access, and customer data protection. Lead customer-impacting incident response and coordinate customer notifications.
  • Security Technology Ownership: Own the security operations technology stack, including SIEM, SOAR, EDR/XDR, cloud detection and response, and log pipelines. Manage the roadmap, budget, and vendor relationships.
  • Threat Hunting & Intelligence: Lead proactive threat hunting and integrate threat intelligence to identify and mitigate emerging threats before they impact the business.
  • Cross-Team Collaboration: Work directly with engineering, infrastructure, IT, application security, and GRC teams to integrate detection and response practices and remediate risks across build pipelines, runtime environments, and corporate systems.
  • Tooling & Automation: Develop and maintain automation, playbooks, and integrations to streamline security processes and provide self-service security tools to the organization.
  • Security Standards & Metrics: Implement consistent security controls, monitoring, and alerting across the enterprise. Define and report on key metrics such as mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to respond (MTTR), and support compliance requirements.
  • Knowledge Sharing: Stay up to date with trends in security operations, incident response, cloud security, and AI security, applying this knowledge to improve the Fivetran platform's security posture.

Skills We’re Looking For

  • Security Operations & Incident Response Expertise: Deep expertise in detecting, investigating, and responding to security incidents, with a track record of leading enterprise-wide incident response.
  • People Management: Proven experience managing, hiring, and developing security teams, including setting priorities, managing performance, and building a strong team culture.
  • Multi-Tenant SaaS Experience: Extensive experience securing and responding to incidents in multi-tenant SaaS environments at scale, with a strong understanding of tenant isolation and customer data protection.
  • AI Proficiency: Hands-on experience applying AI, including LLMs and AI agents, to security operations to automate detection, triage, and response, and a strong understanding of the risks AI introduces.
  • Cloud & Infrastructure Security: Strong experience with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure), Kubernetes, and containerized environments, including cloud-native logging and detection.
  • Detection & Response Tooling: Proficiency with SIEM, SOAR, EDR/XDR, identity, and cloud detection tools, and experience integrating them into automated workflows.
  • Technology Ownership: Experience owning a security technology roadmap, including tool selection, budgets, and vendor management.
  • Problem-Solving: Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to make sound decisions under pressure in fast-paced environments.
  • Communication: Strong communication skills with the ability to effectively collaborate with and educate engineering teams, and to communicate clearly with executives and customers during incidents.
  • Curiosity & Urgency: Demonstrates strong curiosity, a sense of urgency, and a hands-on approach to diving deep into complex technical problems to drive timely and effective solutions.

data.description:
Headquarters: Remote (USA - New York City, NY)

PagerDuty, Inc. (NYSE: PD) is the global leader in AI-first digital operations. By automatically detecting, diagnosing, and remediating issues, the PagerDuty Platform orchestrates AI agents and automated workflows with context from over 750 integrations. Trusted by approximately two-thirds of the Fortune 100 and nearly half of the Fortune 500, PagerDuty is the industry standard for organizations scaling resilient, autonomous operations. Notable customers include Chipotle, Cloudflare, Docusign, Fox, Nvidia, Salesforce, Spotify, Zoom and more. We are growing rapidly and hiring top talent with leading AI skills across engineering, sales, product, marketing, and beyond as we build the leading digital operations platform.

PagerDuty is seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer (SRE Agent) to join our customer-focused SRE Agent team! As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will work inside PagerDuty’s largest customer accounts, connecting the SRE Agent to their production environments (observability tools, infrastructure as code, GitOps tooling, and CI/CD pipelines) and guiding their teams from AI-assisted incident response to supervised and autonomous actions with safety guardrails. You will also contribute code directly back to the core SRE Agent product, building reusable tools, connectors, and skills derived from real customer needs.

This is an exciting opportunity to join the product engineering team as the Staff Engineer and directly shape how agentic AI operates within the most strategic customers. The ideal candidate brings a strong background as a software engineer, hands-on experience shipping LLM/agentic systems to production, and the customer-facing skills to bridge technical execution with business strategy.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 

  • Embed and drive SRE Agent adoption: Work onsite and in regular contact with 2–4 strategic customer teams to deploy the SRE Agent, configure tools and connectors, and embed AI actions across their incident management lifecycle to drive adoption and value 
  • Build and contribute core agent capabilities: Scope, design, and build reusable agent tools, connectors, and skills on the agent’s extensibility surfaces, shipping them through the product team's repos, review process, and evaluation gates.
  • Run pilots and unblock customer adoption: Stand up new agentic capabilities with strategic accounts first, gather eval data, identify technical blockers (permissions, telemetry, missing connectors), and build production fixes directly into the product.
  • Integrate with production stacks and progressive delivery: Connect the SRE Agent to IaC (Terraform, Pulumi), GitOps (ArgoCD), CI/CD pipelines, and observability platforms, guiding customers safely from AI-assisted to autonomous operations.
  • Set technical direction and feedback insights: Define 3–6 month technical roadmaps across assigned accounts, provide architectural guidance to product managers and engineering managers, and bring customer friction and eval data back to the core team.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of experience building and shipping production software across team boundaries (assessed against PagerDuty Staff Engineer / SDE V expectations).
  • Hands-on experience with LLM and agent systems in production, including agent development, tool-use frameworks (MCP or equivalent), evaluation pipelines, and guardrail design.
  • Customer-facing skills. You can run a technical design session with a customer’s engineers and present the business case to their leadership.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity. You can start from a vague problem statement in an unfamiliar environment and get to working software without much direction. Former founders and founding engineers tend to do well in this role.
  • A record of shipping software that got adopted, and the judgment to recognize which customer requests generalize and when the right answer is not to build.
  • Infrastructure & Deployment expertise: Demonstrated experience with Terraform or Pulumi at scale, GitOps (ArgoCD or equivalent), CI/CD pipeline design, and progressive delivery patterns (canary, blue/green, soak periods).
  • Willingness to travel 25–50% during active customer engagements.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Practical operational knowledge of incident management and observability concepts (on-call, postmortems, SLOs/SLIs, alerting).
  • Customer-facing technical consulting, forward-deployed engineering, or solutions architecture experience on top of a core software engineering background.
  • Background as a founder or founding engineer accustomed to navigating high ambiguity and driving unscripted problem-solving.
  • Experience with policy-as-code, fine-grained permissioning, or safety guardrail patterns for agent-driven automation.
  • Production experience with PagerDuty or competing digital operations and incident management platforms.
  • Active open-source contributions to the AI agent or Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem.

The base salary range for this position is $191,000 - $289,300 USD. This role may also be eligible for bonus, commission, equity, and/or benefits.

Job Title: Member of Technical Staff, Infrastructure
